chunks.arabic_text: ٩ - إِبْرَاهِيمُ بْنُ إِسْحَاقَ، الْأَحْمَرِيُّ، يُكْنَى أَبَا إِسْحَاقَ، النَّهَوَنْدِيُّ. فِي حَدِيثِهِ ضَعْفٌ، وَفِي مَذْهَبِهِ ارْتِفَاءٌ. وَيَرْوِي الصَّحِيحَ وَالسَّقِيمَ، وَأَمْرُهُ مُخْتَلِطٌ.

translations.en: 9 – Ibrāhīm b. Isḥāq, al-Aḥmarī, known by the kunya Abū Isḥāq. al-Nahāwandī. In his ḥadīths there is weakness, and in his madhhab there is irtifāʿ. He narrates both the authentic and the weak, and his matter is mixed.

en.summary: This entry from al-Ghadā'irī’s *Kitāb al-Du‘afā* characterizes Ibrāhīm ibn Isḥāq al-Aḥmarī al-Nahāwandī as a narrator of mixed reliability (*mukhtaṭ*), whose hadiths are compromised by weakness (*ḍa‘f*) and whose theological stance is described as 'high' (*irtifā‘*), a term in Shia biographical criticism often indicating elevation in status or sometimes subtle deviation. The description highlights the nuanced evaluation of narrators where both sound and weak reports are transmitted, reflecting the critical scrutiny applied to the chain of transmission (*isnād*) in Shia scholarship.
en.seo_question: Who is Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Ahmarī and what is his status in hadith sciences?
